stem.en: In the absence of a partnership deed, a partner who has advanced a loan to the firm is entitled to interest at:

options.en: No interest

explanation.en: Section 13 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 allows interest at 6% p.a. on a partner's loan when there is no agreement.

stem.en: Under the Companies Act, 2013 and the related Rules, the maximum number of partners in a partnership firm is:

explanation.en: Section 464 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with Rule 10 of the Companies (Miscellaneous) Rules, 2014 limits a firm to 50 partners.

stem.en: Which of the following is NOT an essential feature of partnership?

options.en: Business carried on by all or any of them acting for all
Sharing of profits of a business
Equal capital contribution by all partners
An agreement between partners

explanation.en: Partners may contribute unequal capital or even no capital; equal capital is not required.

stem.en: X and Y have no partnership deed. X lent ₹40,000 to the firm on 1 July 2023. Profit for the year ended 31 March 2024 before interest on the loan is ₹30,000. Y's share of profit is:

explanation.en: Interest on loan = 40,000 × 6% × 9/12 = ₹1,800. Profit left = 28,200, shared equally = ₹14,100 each.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): In the absence of a partnership deed, partners are not entitled to interest on their capitals.
Reason (R): A partnership is based on mutual agency.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is true (Section 13 of the Act). R is also true, but mutual agency is not why interest on capital is denied; the reason is the rule of the Act when there is no agreement.

stem.en: Under the fixed capital method, salary payable to a partner is credited to his:

options.en: Salary account in the ledger of the firm
Capital account
Profit and Loss Account
Current account

explanation.en: Under the fixed method, every item other than permanent capital changes goes to the current account.

stem.en: Under the fixed capital method, which account of a partner can show a debit balance?

options.en: Capital account
Neither account
Current account
Both capital and current accounts

explanation.en: The capital account always shows a credit balance; the current account may be debit if drawings exceed credits.

stem.en: Under the fluctuating capital method: opening capital ₹1,50,000, additional capital ₹20,000, drawings ₹25,000, interest on capital ₹9,000, share of loss ₹12,000. Closing capital is:

A partner's current account (fixed capital method) has an opening credit balance of ₹10,000. During the year: salary ₹18,000, share of profit ₹15,000, drawings ₹36,000, interest on drawings ₹900. Closing balance is:
Net profit of a firm before charging commission is ₹1,32,000. A partner is entitled to a commission of 10% of net profit after charging such commission. The commission is:
Interest on partners' capitals is:

options.en: A charge debited to the Profit and Loss Account
Debited to partners' capital accounts
Credited to the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account
An appropriation debited to the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account

explanation.en: Interest on capital is an appropriation of profit, shown on the debit side of the appropriation account.

stem.en: P and Q have capitals of ₹3,00,000 and ₹2,00,000. The deed allows interest on capital at 10% p.a. as an appropriation. Profit for the year is only ₹40,000. Interest on capital allowed to P will be:

explanation.en: Interest due 30,000 + 20,000 = 50,000 exceeds profit, so the ₹40,000 is shared in the ratio of interest 3:2. P gets ₹24,000.

solution.en: Interest due 30,000 + 20,000 = 50,000 exceeds profit, so the ₹40,000 is shared in the ratio of interest 3:2.

stem.en: A, B and C share profits 2:2:1. Net profit is ₹1,00,000. C gets a salary of ₹20,000, total interest on capital is ₹15,000, and 10% of net profit is transferred to reserve. C's share of the remaining profit is:
What is the divisible profit to be shared by Rohit and Sneha in their profit sharing ratio?

passage.en: Rohit and Sneha are partners sharing profits 3:2. Their capitals are ₹5,00,000 and ₹3,00,000. The deed provides interest on capital at 8% p.a., a salary of ₹2,000 per month to Sneha, and a commission to Rohit of 5% of the net profit before any appropriation. The net profit for the year ended 31 March 2024 is ₹2,00,000.

explanation.en: Interest on capital 40,000 + 24,000; Sneha's salary 24,000; Rohit's commission 5% of 2,00,000 = 10,000. Total 98,000. Divisible profit = 2,00,000 − 98,000 = ₹1,02,000.

stem.en: What is the total amount credited to Sneha (interest, salary and share of profit) from the appropriation account?

passage.en: Rohit and Sneha are partners sharing profits 3:2. Their capitals are ₹5,00,000 and ₹3,00,000. The deed provides interest on capital at 8% p.a., a salary of ₹2,000 per month to Sneha, and a commission to Rohit of 5% of the net profit before any appropriation. The net profit for the year ended 31 March 2024 is ₹2,00,000.

stem.en: A partner draws ₹4,000 at the end of every month. Interest on drawings is 9% p.a. The interest for the year is:

explanation.en: Total 48,000; average period 5.5 months; 48,000 × 9% × 5.5/12 = ₹1,980.

stem.en: A partner draws ₹15,000 at the beginning of each quarter. Interest on drawings is 10% p.a. The interest for the year is:

explanation.en: Total 60,000; average period 7.5 months; 60,000 × 10% × 7.5/12 = ₹3,750.

stem.en: A partner withdrew ₹24,000 during the year; dates are not given. Interest on drawings at 10% p.a. is:

options.en: Nil

explanation.en: When dates are not given, interest is charged for an average of 6 months: 24,000 × 10% × 6/12 = ₹1,200.

stem.en: Interest on drawings charged from partners is:

options.en: Credited to partners' capital accounts
Credited to the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account
Debited to the Profit and Loss Account
Debited to the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account

explanation.en: It is income for the firm: partner's capital/current account Dr, to Interest on Drawings, which is closed to the credit of the appropriation account.

stem.en: X, Y and Z share profits 2:2:1. Z is guaranteed a minimum profit of ₹50,000; any deficiency is to be borne by X alone. Profit is ₹2,00,000. X's final share is:

explanation.en: Z's share = 40,000; deficiency 10,000 borne by X. X = 80,000 − 10,000 = ₹70,000.

stem.en: When a guaranteed partner's actual share of profit is less than the guaranteed amount, the deficiency is borne by:

options.en: All partners equally
The partner(s) who gave the guarantee, in the agreed ratio
The guaranteed partner himself
The firm as an expense in the Profit and Loss Account

explanation.en: The partner(s) who gave the guarantee bear the deficiency in the agreed ratio (their profit sharing ratio if none is agreed).

stem.en: P, Q and R share profits 5:3:2. R is guaranteed ₹60,000, and the deficiency is borne by P and Q equally. Profit is ₹2,40,000. Q's final share is:

explanation.en: R's share = 48,000, deficiency 12,000, borne 6,000 each by P and Q. Q = 72,000 − 6,000 = ₹66,000.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): If the actual share of a guaranteed partner is more than the guaranteed amount, he gets his actual share.
Reason (R): A guarantee only fixes the minimum amount the partner will receive.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: The guarantee is a floor, not a fixed payment, so R correctly explains A.

stem.en: X and Y share profits equally with capitals ₹2,00,000 and ₹1,00,000. After closing the accounts, it is found that interest on capital at 6% p.a. was omitted. The adjustment entry is:

options.en: Y's Capital A/c Dr ₹6,000; To X's Capital A/c ₹6,000
X's Capital A/c Dr ₹3,000; To Y's Capital A/c ₹3,000
Y's Capital A/c Dr ₹3,000; To X's Capital A/c ₹3,000
Profit and Loss Adjustment A/c Dr ₹18,000; To X's and Y's Capital A/cs ₹18,000

explanation.en: Interest X 12,000, Y 6,000; reverse 18,000 equally (9,000 each). Net X +3,000, Y −3,000.

stem.en: Errors and omissions found after the final accounts are closed are corrected through:

options.en: A Profit and Loss Adjustment Account or directly in partners' capital/current accounts
The Trading Account of the next year
The Realisation Account
The Revaluation Account

explanation.en: Past adjustments are made through a Profit and Loss Adjustment Account or by a single entry in partners' capital/current accounts.

stem.en: A, B and C share profits 2:2:1. After closing the accounts it is found that interest on drawings was not charged: A ₹1,000, B ₹600, C ₹400. The adjustment entry is:

options.en: A's Capital A/c Dr ₹200; To C's Capital A/c ₹200
C's Capital A/c Dr ₹400; To A's Capital A/c ₹400
B's Capital A/c Dr ₹200; To A's Capital A/c ₹200
A's Capital A/c Dr ₹200; To B's Capital A/c ₹200

explanation.en: Debit interest on drawings: A 1,000, B 600, C 400. Credit the ₹2,000 in 2:2:1: A 800, B 800, C 400. Net A −200, B +200, C 0.

stem.en: A and B are partners with capitals ₹3,00,000 and ₹2,00,000. The deed allows interest on capital at 8% p.a. (treated as an appropriation). Profit for the year before interest is ₹30,000. How will the profit be distributed?

explanation.en: Interest due: A 24,000 + B 16,000 = ₹40,000, more than the profit of ₹30,000. The whole profit is shared in the ratio of interest, 3:2: A ₹18,000, B ₹12,000.

solution.en: Interest due: A 24,000 + B 16,000 = ₹40,000, more than the profit of ₹30,000.
The whole profit is shared in the ratio of interest, 3:2: A ₹18,000, B ₹12,000.

stem.en: A partner withdraws ₹6,000 at the end of every quarter. Interest on drawings is 10% p.a. The interest on drawings for the year is:

explanation.en: Total drawings = 6,000 × 4 = ₹24,000. End of each quarter: average period 4.5 months. Interest = 24,000 × 10/100 × 4.5/12 = ₹900.

stem.en: X, Y and Z share profits 2:2:1. Z is guaranteed a minimum profit of ₹50,000, any deficiency to be borne by X alone. The firm's profit is ₹2,00,000. X's final share of profit is:
